| ` ` | LF-047 | engine | bug | Threat panel shows base enemy HP, not hp * difficulty multiplier — on hard and brutal every unit is understated (hud.gd:597). The panel is the player's whole read on what is coming, so it should show the HP they will actually shoot at |

| ` ` | LF-049 | art | bug | Hollow lit cones are laterally off-axis from their dark cones, so the emissive collapses at yaw 315. cone() rotates each primitive about its own origin, so two cones sharing rot=(11,-8,0) but sitting at different z have parallel axes offset by ~0.045 world units (~4px): the lit cone pokes out on the +x+y side and hides behind the dark cone from the opposite camera. Measured glow coverage hollow_shard 0.0061 at y315 vs 0.024-0.036 elsewhere; hollow_echo 0.0089 vs 0.042-0.068. Currently latent because anchor_view.gd only ever draws y045 (see the sibling item). Fix is to put the lit cone on the dark cone's rotated axis, or to build both from one origin, and it applies to the whole Hollow set at once rather than shard alone |
| ` ` | LF-052 | engine | feature | Board camera: pan and zoom. Pan on middle-drag plus lf_* keys and edge-scroll, NOT left-drag — left click arms builds and selects emplacements, so drag-to-pan turns every slipped click into a camera move. The board cursor should carry the camera with it, which gives keyboard and gamepad panning without a second system. Zoom transforms the BOARD LAYER ONLY: the HUD ladder and palette were solved for WCAG AA at a known size (045/046) and scaling them with the board silently undoes it. Zoom out is cheap; zoom in past 1.0 softens sprites, which are a fixed 256px atlas at one orthographic scale, so either raise the render base or clamp. Value is inspection on a busy board, not navigation — a 17x13 grid already fits — so it must never be required to play. Needs a --camera x,y,zoom verification hook or every --shot/--a11y report becomes camera-state dependent |
| ` ` | LF-053 | design | chore | standard_policies() cannot express a mixed board: every Policy is a total preference order and _try_build fills every free slot greedily from the top, so a graded build is all-of-one-thing. 'Three pulse turrets in front of an ion lance' is not in the search space, which makes claims like 'the escort brings the cheap emplacements back' unfalsifiable by the harness that is supposed to test them. Needs capped-core policies (cap the expensive tower at N, fill the rest cheap) |
| ` ` | LF-054 | design | bug | PRESSURE_FLOOR in sim/run.py is a dead check: peak load ratio is >=100% of capacity on all 24 anchors x 3 difficulties, and still >=75% everywhere with the greedy-overdraw policy excluded, so 'the player is pressed against capacity' can never fail. Either measure pressure on winning builds only, or raise the floor until it discriminates |
| ` ` | LF-055 | engine | bug | anchor_sim._step's splash loop tests 'u == target' but Godot 4.7 compares Dictionary by value (probed: two dicts with equal contents are ==, and Array.find matches by value), while sim/engine.py tests 'u is target'. Two units of the same kind with equal hp and equal dist therefore drop out of splash damage in GDScript and take it in Python. Latent only because same-kind units spawn on different ticks so their dist differs — a wave table that spawns two identical units on the same tick turns it into a parity failure. Found while deciding where facing state could live (LF-050); the fix is an identity-safe test on the GDScript side, e.g. comparing by index |
| ` ` | LF-056 | tooling | chore | Running the editor import (godot --headless --path . --import) rewrote scripts/menu.gd from tab indentation to four-space indentation, a 442-line no-op diff that has to be reverted by hand before committing. | LF-044 | design | Act II/III density: decision 047 removed the blocker, now spend it — re-author Act II/III wave composition for more, lighter units at constant wave leak_cost, then re-sweep anchors 09-24 | done — PREMISE RE-MEASURED 2026-07-28; the original note was wrong on all three counts.
1. The roster is not the constraint: ~0.52 dps/MW against shielded/armoured vs ~1.0 against plain is a 2x penalty, not an absence. The proposed mid-cost anti-armour emplacement would not have helped.
2. Throughput is not the constraint: 2x damage on every weapon AND +60% capacity (3.2x throughput) still reaches only 1/11 winning builds at weight 1.50 on anchor-20.
3. 'Does not grade clean at any life count' was false — anchor-20 at weight 1.50 grades clean at 72 lives. Never tested: sweep.py defaults to weights [0.85, 1.0, 1.15] and the anchor's current life count.

ROOT CAUSE, now fixed by decision 047: density and leak-tension were the same axis, because a leak cost one life whether it was a 22 hp mote or a 520 hp Column. leak_cost = max(1, round(hp/130)) makes trading one Column for four ~130 hp units tension-neutral.

REMAINING WORK, mechanical and not blocked on the owner: re-author Act II and III wave composition to field more, lighter units in place of the bricks, holding each wave's total leak_cost roughly where it is, then re-sweep anchors 09-24. Judge the result on leak budget (lives / total leak_cost), not on raw lives — Act I sits at 8.7%, Act II 18.0%, Act III 30.4%. |
